newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT loses one bln pesos/yr on call scheme.
newsitem.headline: PLDT loses one bln pesos/yr on call scheme.

text.p: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co (PLDT) said on Monday it was losing more than one billion pesos every year from overseas calling arrangements which skirt around PLDT's international call services.

"The existence of alternative international calling arrangements, such as call- back services, international simple resale and Internet telephony, contribute immensely to the haemorrhage in PLDT's international call revenues," Miguela Villanueva, PLDT's head of pricing division, said in her petition to the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC).
The alternative schemes offer local rates or sharply reduced rates to its subscribers by using certain devices to avoid PLDT's detection of their call traffic.
"It is estimated that on the average the loss resulting from such reaches more than one billiopn pesos annually," she added.
PLDT is petitioning for a restructuring of its tariff schedules, asking the NTC to increase its local and domestic long distance rates to offset a possible cut in international call rates.
The US Federal Communications Commission has been pushing for a drastic reduction in the cost of international calls over the next two years.

"The only way to minimise such alternative calling arrangements and the resultant loss to PLDT and other IGF operators is to reduce the gap between international collection rates in the Philippines and the rates these alternative calling providers charge," she added.
